implemented_requirements.evidence: class Board: ... self.grid = [[EMPTY_CELL for _ in range(3)] for _ in range(3)]

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players alternate placing X or O
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.current_player returns the player at current_player_index; Game.switch_player flips the index; Game.make_move calls self.switch_player() when the move is legal and the round is not over.
Board.get_winning_line(symbol) checks rows, columns, and diagonals and returns a line; Game.make_move sets self.winner and self.winning_line when a line is found.
Board.grid stores the symbols; Player object holds name, symbol, and win count; Game.board is shared between moves.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when a player wins or the board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.make_move sets self.game_over = True on a win or when board.is_full() returns True; get_status() reports win or draw.

console_ui.run_console_game() provides prompts, board rendering, and quit handling; gui.TicTacToeGUI builds a Tkinter window with clickable cells, status label, score label, and pop‑up result messages.

judge.summary: All core features of a two‑player tic‑tac‑toe game are present: a 3x3 board, move validation, turn alternation, win/draw detection, score tracking, and both a console and a Tkinter GUI. The code is self‑contained and appears ready to run, so the submission meets the benchmark.
